Right: the same square plus the diagonal 1 to 3, in the accent color, which closes the triangles 1, 2, 3 and 1, 3, 4; odd closed walks now count against it and the value drops to 0.795." width="100%"} Estrada and Rodríguez-Velázquez (2005) weigh every closed walk by $1 / k!$ for its length $k$: a graph is bipartite exactly when it has no closed walks of odd length, so the share of even closed walks, $\mathrm{tr}\cosh(A) / \mathrm{tr}\, e^{A}$, equals 1 for bipartite graphs and drops toward 1/2 as odd cycles (triangles above all) take over. It grades "almost bipartite" networks, such as protein interaction or food webs with a two-mode backbone. Per-node values show which nodes take part in odd cycles. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [nodes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Union[int, str]] | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional nodes (IDs or labels): return each node's own bipartivity, $\cosh(A)_{ii} / (e^A)_{ii}$, instead of the graph value. [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to use edge weights in $A$. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [float or dict[int, float]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The graph's bipartivity (between 1/2 and 1), or a node-to-value dictionary. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or a node does not exist. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The matrix functions are evaluated from one symmetric eigendecomposition $A = V \Lambda V^\top$: $(e^A)_{ii} = \sum_k V_{ik}^2 e^{\lambda_k}$ and likewise with $\cosh$, in $O(n^3)$ time. Matches NetworkX's `bipartite.spectral_bipartivity` (which uses `scipy.linalg.expm`). ## Examples {.doc-examples} A square is perfectly bipartite; adding one diagonal creates triangles: ::: {#ea2c91ff .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec square = ec.Graph().add_cycle_graph(4) before = square.spectral_bipartivity() ids = sorted(square.get_node_ids(limit=None)) square.add_edge(ids[0], ids[2]) before, round(square.spectral_bipartivity(), 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1.0, 0.795) ``` ::: :::
